Oncology
At Animal Samaritans, we understand how frightening a cancer diagnosis can be—for you and for your beloved pet. Early diagnosis improves outcomes, so if you’ve noticed a persistent lump, abnormal swelling or unexplained weight loss in your dog or cat, we encourage you to schedule an evaluation promptly.
Our dedicated oncology team provides
pet cancer treatment
, including
dog oncology and cancer care
and
cat oncology and cancer care
, using the latest diagnostic tools and therapies. We offer
tumor testing
,
lump removal
, and customized
chemotherapy
programs tailored to your animal’s needs. We also offer a new,
less-invasive
therapy,
vetIQure™ Tumour Specific Electroporation (TSE)
, an advanced, targeted therapy designed to enhance the delivery of therapeutic agents directly into cancer cells while minimizing effects on surrounding healthy tissue.
Our goal is to give your pet the best chance at a longer, higher-quality life through compassionate, expert care.
For more information you can call 760-332-5030 or email
oncology@animalsamaritans.org
To make an Oncology appointment please call 760-332-5030
What to Expect: Customized Oncology Services for Pets
Staging (Additional Diagnostics)
After a diagnosis of cancer, additional diagnostic testing can help to determine the extent of cancer in the body, which allows us to optimize treatment recommendations and better predict prognosis.
Treatment Options
When staging is complete our team of specialists will discuss all the appropriate treatment options. Cancer can be treated by several different therapies or combination of treatments including surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapies or palliative care when appropriate.
What is vetIQure™ Tumour Specific Electroporation (TSE)?
Animal Samaritans Veterinary Specialists offers vetIQure™ Tumour Specific Electroporation (TSE), an advanced, targeted therapy designed to enhance the delivery of therapeutic agents directly into cancer cells while minimizing effects on surrounding healthy tissue. Using precisely controlled electrical pulses, TSE temporarily increases tumor cell permeability, allowing medications to enter more effectively and support a localized treatment approach. This technology promotes a controlled cellular response (apoptosis) rather than indiscriminate tissue destruction.
Why choose vetIQure™ Tumour Specific Electroporation (TSE)?
TSE may be considered for tumors in sensitive or surgically challenging locations, when clear surgical margins are difficult to achieve, or as part of a comprehensive cancer care plan.
Our board-certified oncology team carefully evaluates each patient to determine whether TSE is appropriate, ensuring a personalized and compassionate approach to your pet’s cancer treatment.
Meet our Oncologist
Vincent Baldanza, VMD, DACVIM
Dr. Vincent Baldanza, VMD, DACVIM
Dr. Vincent Baldanza was born and raised in northern New Jersey. He graduated Summa Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Science from the University of Delaware, where he studied Animal Science and spent semesters studying abroad in Australia and Italy.
Dr. Baldanza graduated Magna Cum Laude with a Doctorate of Veterinary Medicine from the University of Pennsylvania. After graduating from veterinary school, Dr. Baldanza completed a one-year small animal rotating internship at the University of Minnesota and a three-year residency in medical oncology at Cornell University, where he was selected as an American Kennel Club Canine Health Foundation Clinician-Scientist Fellow for his research in canine osteosarcoma.
Upon completion of his studies, Dr. Baldanza moved to Los Angeles to work with the Veterinary Cancer Group and ACCESS specialty hospitals for several years. Dr. Baldanza is a board-certitied specialist in medical oncology and his special interests include blood cancers, novel therapeutics, and palliative care.
Outside of work, Dr. Baldanza enjoys life in the desert with his husband, their dogs, cats, and tortoise.
For an appointment with Dr. Baldanza, call our Oncology department at
760-332-5030
, or email
oncology@animalsamaritans.org
